title: Audit Logging Program Overview (Schema v1 + Sensitive Action Coverage)
author: Naomi Feldman
body:
## Purpose
This page is the top-level overview for Redwood Inference’s audit logging program. The program standardizes **what we log**, **how we log it**, and **how we prove coverage** for customer- and auditor-facing requirements across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

This overview is intended for:
- Engineering teams instrumenting services
- Security Engineering and GRC validating controls
- SRE and Platform teams operating the audit-log pipeline and exporters
- Product/CS/Sales needing consistent, supportable statements about audit logging

## Program goals
1) **Canonical, versioned schema** for audit events (stable, validated, backwards-compatible)
2) **100% coverage** for defined “sensitive actions” across in-scope systems
3) **Operational reliability**: measurable delivery lag SLO, retries, and exporter hardening
4) **Customer usability**: searchable audit log UI/API and export options (S3/SIEM/webhook)
5) **Compliance alignment**: SOC 2 / ISO-friendly evidence, retention/redaction guidance

## Non-goals (initial scope)
- Logging all observability/product analytics events (only audit-relevant security/administrative events)
- Sampling (audit logs are not sampled)
- Full historical backfill of all legacy logs (limited migration/backfill only where contractually required)
- Supporting customer-defined custom schemas (we provide canonical schema + export formats)

## Definition: “Sensitive action”
A **sensitive action** is any action that materially impacts one or more of:
- **Customer data access** (read/export/delete access, permission changes, key issuance)
- **Security posture** (auth/RBAC changes, org security settings, audit config changes)
- **Billing/quotas/capacity entitlements** (quota changes, committed capacity changes)
- **Availability / serving behavior** for customer workloads (deployment/rollout/routing changes)

A sensitive action must produce one or more audit events that:
- are emitted at the time the system accepts/attempts the action
- include actor attribution and request correlation
- encode outcome semantics (success/failure) and error details safely
- are delivered to the audit-log store/export with defined reliability guarantees

See the inventory and mapping table for the authoritative list and expected events:
- **Sensitive Actions Inventory + Mapping**: `security-and-compliance/audit-logging/sensitive-actions-inventory-and-mapping`

## In-scope actions (examples)
The following categories are in-scope for schema v1 and coverage enforcement:
- Auth/RBAC changes (roles, permissions, policy bundles)
- API key creation / rotation / revocation
- User/admin management (invite, deactivate, role assignment)
- Org/workspace settings that affect security or access
- Model deployment and rollout actions (canary start/stop, pin/unpin, fallback/routing policy changes)
- Dedicated capacity scaling and quota/admin changes (manual vs auto)
- Private deployment install/upgrade/rollback actions
- Data retention changes
- Audit log configuration changes (export sinks, retention tiers, filters)

## In-scope systems and services
Audit logging is cross-surface; instrumentation must be consistent across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.

| Surface | Primary components (examples) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Hosted API | API Gateway, Auth/RBAC service, Control Plane services | Must propagate `request_id` and actor through gateway → downstream services |
| Console | Console Backend, Admin APIs, RBAC checks | UI triggers must be auditable; backend is source of truth for auditing |
| Dedicated | Dedicated Control Plane, Capacity Manager, Quota Service | Include before/after desired capacity and initiator (auto/manual) |
| Private | Private Installer, Upgrade Controller, Private Control Plane | Must capture operator identity + cluster identifiers; support air-gapped constraints |
| Audit pipeline | Ingest → validate → store → export | Enforces schema validation and delivery semantics |

System-level architecture and failure modes:
- **Audit Log Pipeline Service**: `eng-platform/systems-and-services/audit-log-pipeline-service`

## Canonical schema (v1)
All teams must use the canonical schema and shared libraries.
- **Audit Event Schema v1**: `security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-event-schema-v1`

Schema highlights (see schema page for full requirements):
- Required envelope fields include `event_name`, `event_version`, `occurred_at`, `org`, `actor`, `target`, `request_id`, `ip`, `user_agent`, and `outcome`
- Actor model supports end-user actors and service principals (controllers/automation)
- Outcome encodes success/failure, with safe error semantics (no secrets)
- Versioning strategy supports additive changes and controlled deprecations

Event naming conventions:
- **Audit Event Naming Guidelines**: `architecture-and-standards/api-standards/audit-event-naming-guidelines`

## Coverage: what “100%” means
Coverage is measured against the **Sensitive Actions Inventory**.

An action is considered “covered” when:
1) The action is present in the inventory (with owner/team and expected event(s))
2) Instrumented code emits the expected event(s) on all code paths (including error paths where applicable)
3) Emitted events pass schema validation (locally or in the pipeline) and are persisted
4) Integration tests exist for the action class, and CI gates pass

Coverage policy details, CI enforcement, and exception process:
- **Coverage Policy and Enforcement**: `security-and-compliance/audit-logging/coverage-policy-and-enforcement`

## Reliability and telemetry requirements
Audit logs are security controls; reliability is mandatory and measurable.

Telemetry standards define:
- Correlation IDs and propagation (`request_id`, trace/span linkage where available)
- Retry semantics and backpressure behavior
- Metrics naming (enqueue/persist/export counts) and delivery lag histogram
- Definition of “drop” vs “delay” and alerting thresholds

References:
- **Audit Log Telemetry Standards**: `architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/audit-log-telemetry-standards`
- **Audit Log Delivery Lag Runbook**: `eng-sre/runbooks/audit-log-delivery-lag-runbook`

## Security: threat model + controls
The audit log system must be resilient against:
- Tampering (modification of events)
- Bypass (sensitive actions with no events)
- Spoofing (incorrect actor attribution)
- PII leakage (over-logging sensitive fields)

Controls include:
- Schema validation and strict required-field enforcement
- Append-only storage properties (where applicable) and access controls
- Redaction rules (no secrets/tokens); safe error reporting
- Restricted internal access and monitoring of internal queries

References:
- **Audit Log Threat Model**: `security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-log-threat-model`
- **Audit Log Access Policy**: `policies-and-process/access-and-permissions/audit-log-access-policy`

## Migration plan (legacy → schema v1)
We are migrating legacy/partial audit events via:
- Dual-write (legacy event names + schema v1 names) for a defined window
- Deprecation warnings and cutover flags per environment
- Customer-facing change notes where required

Reference:
- **Legacy Event Migration Plan**: `security-and-compliance/audit-logging/legacy-event-migration-plan`

## Rollout phases and timeline (typical ~2 quarters)
1) **Discovery + inventory (2–3 weeks)**
   - Enumerate sensitive actions across surfaces
   - Audit existing logging + identify gaps
   - Define acceptance criteria per action category

2) **Schema v1 + shared libraries (3–5 weeks)**
   - Publish schema v1 + examples
   - Implement validators and developer guidance
   - Establish event registry and naming enforcement

3) **Instrumentation + migration (6–10 weeks)**
   - Service-by-service instrumentation
   - Normalize legacy events; dual-write where required
   - Add automated tests and fix missing code paths

4) **Reliability + reporting (3–6 weeks)**
   - Delivery lag SLO, dashboards, alerts
   - Exporter hardening (retries, DLQ, per-sink metrics)
   - Coverage reports per subsystem

5) **Beta + launch (3–6 weeks)**
   - Enable enterprise design partners
   - Security review collateral and runbook training
   - GA rollout with release readiness gates

## Dashboards, reports, and how to measure success
Success is tracked with:
- Coverage % by subsystem and action category (target: 100% for in-scope actions)
- Delivery lag SLO attainment and drop rate (target defined in telemetry standards)
- Exporter success rates by sink type (S3/SIEM/webhook)
- Supportability metrics: number of audit-log-related escalations and time-to-diagnose

Primary artifacts:
- Sensitive action inventory and coverage mapping (source of truth): `security-and-compliance/audit-logging/sensitive-actions-inventory-and-mapping`
- Coverage policy and CI enforcement: `security-and-compliance/audit-logging/coverage-policy-and-enforcement`
- Operational telemetry standards + runbook: `architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/audit-log-telemetry-standards` and `eng-sre/runbooks/audit-log-delivery-lag-runbook`

## Compliance mapping and evidence
GRC maintains the mapping from audit logging requirements to SOC 2/ISO evidence expectations, including:
- Which schema fields substantiate key controls
- How we generate auditor-friendly exports (sample queries, retention settings)
- Evidence collection procedure and sign-off

Reference:
- **Audit Logging Control Mapping (SOC 2/ISO)**: `security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/audit-logging-control-mapping-soc2`

## Customer-facing requirements
Product requirements and go-to-market guidance live here:
- **Enterprise PRD**: `product-docs/requirements/audit-logs-enterprise-prd`
- **Sales/SE FAQ**: `sales-enablement/security-faq/audit-logs-faq`

## How to add a new sensitive action (process)
1) Add the action to the **Sensitive Actions Inventory + Mapping** with:
   - Clear action name and description
   - Owning team/service
   - Expected audit event name(s) and trigger points
   - Notes on target/actor modeling and redaction

2) Implement instrumentation using the shared audit logging library and event registry.

3) Add/extend integration tests to assert:
   - event exists
   - required fields are present
   - outcome semantics are correct for both success and failure scenarios

4) Ensure CI coverage gates pass (or file a time-bound exception per policy).

## Open questions / upcoming decisions
- Final GA SLO targets for delivery lag per region and per sink type (baseline is tracked in SRE working docs; final targets will be published in telemetry standards)
- Retention defaults by plan tier and export entitlements (tracked in Product packaging decision)
- Standardization of “diff” payloads for policy changes across subsystems (RBAC vs deployment policies)
